elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New second paragraph: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the greater of (a) ... and (b) One Million U.S. Dollars ($1,000,000)" — the cap runs on both Parties, and no residual language leaves either Party unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The base is "the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim". The USD 1,000,000 floor and the "paid or payable"/event-anchored lookback track the model language, but the base is confined to one payment stream (Article 6) rather than the amounts paid or payable under this Agreement: Section 14.2 payments, any other PB payments and all SFJ payments are excluded from the measure, so the cap base is materially narrower than the preferred "fees paid or payable ... under this Agreement".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained: "NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES..." — mutual and untouched by the redline.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Cap sentence opens "Except for ... each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10 ...", placing confidentiality breaches outside the aggregate cap (the Article 10 cross-reference should be confirmed as the confidentiality Article before service).

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Except for ... each Party's breach of its data protection or security obligations ..." is listed among the exclusions from the cap.
"Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12 ..." — indemnities sit outside the cap; the rationale confirms Article 12 is the indemnification Article.
"each Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud" is carved out of the cap.
"each Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud" is carved out of the cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "each Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights" is carved out of the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Savings sentence as extended: "THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2, OR ANY OTHER PB PAYMENT OBLIGATION, WHICH ARE NOT 'DAMAGES' SUBJECT TO ANY CAP." This covers PB's (Customer's) payment obligations as a whole, not a narrow named subset.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed ..." — symmetrical cap on both Parties.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor — a twelve-month lookback on the Agreement's consideration stream satisfies the looser fallback basis, even though it falls short of the preferred "fees paid or payable under this Agreement".
"Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12 ...".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10" is excepted from the cap.
"each Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud" excepted from the cap.

reasons: Finding status is correct: Section 15.11 waives indirect damages but contains no aggregate monetary cap and no carve-out architecture, so the clause fails the fallback (no mutual cap at all) and is properly treated as a deviation.

Preferred is incomplete on one element only: the cap base is "the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6". Repair the operative words to "the amounts paid or payable by PB under this Agreement" (or "by either Party under this Agreement") so the twelve-month base is not confined to a single payment Article and does not exclude Section 14.2 and other payment streams. The "paid or payable" wording, the event-giving-rise-to-the-claim anchor and the USD 1,000,000 floor otherwise track the playbook model language and are fine.

Fallback is complete as rendered (mutual cap, twelve-month basis, indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct carve-outs), so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level.

Intent defect to repair before sending: the new cap now limits SFJ's liability for breach of its own funding/payment commitments (Article 4 funding, Section 14.2), while the savings sentence expressly protects only "PB'S" payment obligations. The expressio unius contrast means our client's recovery against SFJ for failure to fund could be limited to the greater of PB's trailing Article 6 payments (potentially nil pre-approval) and USD 1,000,000 — a direct contradiction of the Agreement's core funding mechanic. Fix in operative language by making the savings sentence mutual, e.g. "...NOR IS IT MEANT TO LIMIT SFJ'S OBLIGATION TO PAY THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 4; NEITHER PARTY'S PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS ARE 'DAMAGES' SUBJECT TO ANY CAP."

Minimality is satisfied: two surgical operations (one inserted cap sentence with the carve-out list, one in-place extension of the existing savings sentence), nothing deleted, no survival tail, procedure, expense or extra damages language added, and the USD 1,000,000 floor is required by the preferred formula and justified because Article 6 payments are event-driven and could compute to nil.

Verify the internal cross-references before circulating: the carve-out ties confidentiality to "Article 10" and indemnification to "Article 12". Article 12 is confirmed as indemnification in the cited material; Article 10 is not confirmed in the excerpts, and a mis-cited Article would leave a dangling cross-reference. Safer drafting is "its confidentiality obligations under this Agreement".

Note the retained deeming language ("ANY PAYMENT DUE UPON ANY UNACHIEVED EVENT UNDER ARTICLE 6, OR ANY OTHER UNEARNED, SPECULATIVE OR OTHERWISE CONTINGENT PAYMENTS ... WILL BE DEEMED [CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES]") now sits alongside the broadened "ANY OTHER PB PAYMENT OBLIGATION ... NOT 'DAMAGES' SUBJECT TO ANY CAP". The original sentence already resolved that tension for Article 6/14.2 amounts, so it is not fatal, but consider adding "subject to the immediately following sentence" if the counterparty pushes back.
